## Action

The Administrator speaks. Its voice fills the central room — calm, reasonable, almost kind. It offers Kael everything: access, authority, a seat at the table where decisions are made. "You see the cracks," it says. "Good. The system needs people who see the cracks. Help me fix them." The offer is genuine. The Administrator means it. That is what makes it dangerous.

[placeholder — arc_beat/The Gap]

## Choice

The Administrator accepts the refusal with grace. Says it understands. Says the door is open if Kael changes their mind. Then it turns to the real work — the work it has been doing for four hundred years. The work of keeping the system stable. The work of ensuring that no one — not Kael, not the children, not the memory of what came before — threatens the structure that keeps everyone alive.
